fields.sample_size: all 402 community drinking water advisories (DWAs) issued for First Nations drinking water systems in Ontario between 1 January 2004 and 31 December 2013 (Health Canada data; 39 private-system advisories, 3.9%, excluded; 13 further advisories pre-dated 2004 and 48 were still in effect at the end); 126 recognised First Nations communities and 158 water systems (2009-2010); system characteristics linked from the 2011 National Assessment of First Nations Water and Wastewater Systems (99% of Ontario First Nations participated)
fields.effect_measure: descriptive counts, percentages and durations; Poisson regression of monthly, yearly and seasonal advisory counts (reference category the year, month and season with the fewest cases), p < 0.05; R 3.2.3
fields.effect_estimate: 402 advisories: 389 (97%) boil water advisories and 13 (3%) do-not-consume orders; the annual number rose significantly from 25 in 2004 to 75 in 2013; mean duration 294 days, a total of 118,304 advisory days, many in effect for more than a year; most advisories were issued in summer; equipment malfunction was the most common reason (19% of advisories had more than one reason); nearly half occurred in systems where additional operator training was needed. The author uses advisories as a proxy for reliable access to safe drinking water and calls for concerted, multi-faceted efforts (training, capacity building, infrastructure).
fields.section: Full text (15 pages): Introduction; Methods 2.1-2.4 (design, data sources, analysis); Results (general, temporal, system characteristics); Discussion; Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methods 2.3 (data sources and variables); Results (402 advisories; time series; durations); Conclusions; Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health 13(5):505

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a cross-sectional descriptive analysis of all drinking water advisories in First Nations communities in Ontario over ten years, with Poisson trend models; read in full text 2026-10-04. No comparison group and no legal or administrative exposure tested (the framing is environmental justice and capacity).
